decisions.reason: The legacy claim has no machine-enforceable fitment or persisted product-identity evidence; the newly reviewed scoped 20-2403 candidate must replace it through a guarded merge.

sourceEvidence.title: Loss of Power Steering Assist (Pump Wear)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the power steering pump (and inspect/replace fluid and lines). Covered under GM Special Coverage for 10yr/150k mi on affected vehicles; otherwise replace the pump out of pocket.

decisions.reason: The legacy WPGM-611V claim is unscoped and lacks persisted product-identity evidence; the newly reviewed 2008-2017 candidate is the safe replacement.

sourceEvidence.title: Water Pump Leak / Coolant Loss on 3.6L V6
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the water pump (and thermostat/gasket as needed), then refill and bleed the cooling system. A relatively common, moderate-cost repair on these vehicles.

decisions.reason: The current 82-1005AR claim has no door or side scope even though regulator assemblies are position-specific, so it can expose a wrong application.

sourceEvidence.title: Power Window Regulator Cable Failure (Windows Drop or Stop Working)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the failed window regulator assembly with an updated aftermarket unit (commonly available for $50-$100); the motor can usually be reused. Many owners replace regulators in remaining doors preemptively or keep a spare, since failures across all four windows are widely reported.

decisions.reason: FG0347 was confirmed only for 2000-2005 while the frozen issue spans earlier years; the unscoped public claim can therefore show outside proven fitment.

sourceEvidence.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump and Fuel Level Sender Failure (Stalling, No-Start, Erratic Gauge)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the complete fuel pump module assembly (pump, sender, and strainer together) — the tank must be dropped on these cars. Replacing the whole module rather than just the pump fixes the erratic fuel gauge at the same time.

decisions.reason: The legacy DP986 claim lacks persisted engine/year fitment and product-identity evidence; the newly reviewed 1994-1996 LT1 candidate must replace it through the guarded merge.

sourceEvidence.title: Optispark (Opti-Spark) distributor failure on the LT1
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the Optispark with an AC Delco (vented) unit, and because the water pump has to come off to access it, replace the water pump at the same time. Ensure the distributor vent hoses are correctly routed and clear so condensation can escape. Rule out spark plug wires and plugs first, as those often mimic Optispark failure.
